email.subject: New sign-in to your TeamChat account

body.v: We noticed a sign-in to your TeamChat account from a new device in another country. If this was not you, please secure your account within the next few hours.
Thank you for helping us keep TeamChat safe.

hotspots.explain: teamchat-support.example is not TeamChat's domain, teamchat.example. Anyone can register a name that sounds official.
A sign-in from abroad and "the next few hours" are meant to scare you into acting fast.
The button leads to teamchat-secure.example, a different domain from the real one.
Signatures are easy to copy. This one proves nothing either way.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Someone pretending to be TeamChat. The name looks right, but the address is on teamchat-support.example, not teamchat.example.
choices: Someone using an address that only looks like TeamChat's

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: Fear and hurry: a stranger may be in your account and you must act within hours.
choices: None: it is a routine notice
Fear that someone is in your account, with a rush

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Click the link and sign in, which would hand your login to the sender.
choices: Nothing, it is only for information
Click a link and sign in

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Ignore the link. Open the TeamChat app yourself and look at your devices and recent sign-ins.
choices: Click the link to see whether it is real
Reply and ask if the alert is genuine
Open the TeamChat app yourself and check your devices

actions.label: Open the TeamChat app yourself and check your devices
actions.consequence: Only your own devices are listed. The alert was fake.

actions.label: Click "Secure my account" and sign in
actions.consequence: The page looks like TeamChat, but your login goes straight to the scammer.

actions.label: Reply and ask whether the alert is real
actions.consequence: The scammer says yes and pushes harder. Your reply also shows your address is in use.

actions.label: Report it as phishing and delete it

attacker_reveal: A made-up alert, a foreign country and a few hours to decide... Fear does half my work. The address was close enough that you had to read every letter to catch it.
